title: A Mysterious Sniper Murder Case
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Ran, Kogoro Mouri, Inspector Megure, Takagi) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed, attributed edge between the entities involved. case_type: murder. Two distinct false accusations occur before the reveal: Shibata (real grudge motive against Ishimoto, but a solid alibi) is accused first, then the detective sets a deliberate trap by publicly accusing Ishimoto himself to provoke the true culprit, Niikura, into a slip of the tongue about where the remote was found. Both are preserved as has_motive_against / accusation material distinct from the true culprit's motive.

clues.desc: The spotlight lighting Takada's path to the stage was designed to automatically track the wireless microphone clipped to his chest. Since the rigged gun (o1) was mounted on that exact light fixture, the shooter never needed line of sight on the crowd -- they only needed to time a remote trigger for the moment Takada's tracked position drew level with Ishimoto.

Niikura, presenting himself as having independently found evidence, said only that the remote was recovered 'at Ishimoto's company' -- he never specified which room. Yet he referred to it as having come from Ishimoto's presidential office specifically, information only the person who hid it there could have known.

The remote's outer casing had been wiped clean, but its battery had not: Niikura personally reinserted it bare-handed after dropping the remote during a business-card exchange the night of the party, leaving his own fingerprints on the one part he'd overlooked.
